sections.content: Sometimes you want to add something that is not part of your main line: a detail that has just come to mind, or a comment on the side. Spanish has set phrases that tell the listener "this is a side remark", and one that tells them "now I am back". *Por cierto* ("by the way") brings in a new thought loosely connected to what you were saying. *A propósito* also means "by the way", and *a propósito de* + noun means "speaking of": the remark is triggered by something just mentioned. *Dicho sea de paso* ("incidentally", literally "said in passing") fits a short comment, often between commas inside a sentence. To go back, use *volviendo a lo que decíamos* ("going back to what we were saying").

sections.title: Side remarks and the way back
rows: Mañana tengo una reunión. Por cierto, ¿tienes el informe?
I have a meeting tomorrow. By the way, do you have the report?
By the way, have you already bought the tickets?
A propósito de la reunión, ¿a qué hora empieza?
Speaking of the meeting, what time does it start?
La oficina, dicho sea de paso, está muy cerca de mi casa.
The office, incidentally, is very close to my house.
Volviendo a lo que decíamos, ¿quién presenta el informe?
Going back to what we were saying, who presents the report?

sections.content: A side remark is short, and you should come back to the main line afterwards. You know *además* from A2 Unit 28: use it, not these phrases, to add a main point. *Volviendo* is the gerund of *volver*, and *decíamos* is the *imperfecto* of *decir* with *nosotros*.
